title: Monoidal flat model for unbounded complexes on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Write $\mathcal A_R=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ for its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A_R)$ for its unbounded cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Here a combinatorial differential graded model category means a locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups (with cochain differentials and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]), with cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences satisfying two-out-of-three, closure under retracts, and functorial factorizations into (cofibration, trivial fibration) and (trivial cofibration, fibration), with the corresponding lifting properties. The two weak factorization systems are generated by sets. Enrichment satisfies the model compatibility axiom: for a cofibration $i$ and a fibration $p$, the induced map of Hom complexes is a fibration in the projective model structure on complexes of abelian groups, trivial if $i$ or $p$ is trivial. Trivial means also a weak equivalence. Stable means that the enhanced localization has a zero object and finite homotopy limits and colimits, and its homotopy pushout squares are exactly its homotopy pullback squares. A differential graded Quillen adjunction is an enriched adjunction whose left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Its enhanced localization retains derived mapping complexes and all composition homotopies; equivalently one may use the associated stable homotopy theory with its chain enrichment when the model category is stable.

There is a stable combinatorial differential graded model structure on $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A_R)$ whose weak equivalences are exactly the quasi-isomorphisms and whose cofibrations are exactly the termwise monomorphisms with K-flat, termwise flat cokernel [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Thus its cofibrant objects are exactly the K-flat complexes with flat terms. Its ordinary homotopy category is the unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A_R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the complex of internal sheaf Homs [def-pur-sheaf-hom] give a closed symmetric monoidal model structure: the tensor unit $R[0]$ is cofibrant, the pushout product of two cofibrations is a cofibration, and it is trivial if either factor is trivial. Here closed means tensor in each variable has the internal-Hom right adjoint; the complex of internal Homs has degree $r$ equal to $\prod_p\mathcal Hom_R(P^p,Q^{p+r})$ and differential $h\mapsto d_Qh-(-1)^rh d_P$. Fibrations and the two functorial factorizations are part of the asserted model structure; no enough-projectives hypothesis or flatness assumption on a later coefficient homomorphism is imposed.
